leftEvidence.title: John denies three identities and names a present unknown one

points.label: Event action and claim
points.left: John tells Jerusalem’s delegation that he is not the Christ, Elijah, or the prophet, then identifies himself with Isaiah’s voice.
points.right: John calls Jesus God’s Lamb, says Jesus ranks before him, and explains that the purpose of his water baptism was Israel’s recognition.

points.label: Response and consequence
points.left: He explains his water baptism by pointing to one already standing among them.
points.right: John testifies that he saw the Spirit descend and remain, receiving that sign from the one who sent him.

payload.posture: Successive scenes move from John’s denied identities to his positive witness about Jesus.

rightEvidence.title: John identifies Jesus by a descending and remaining Spirit

payload.tension: John names what he is not before explaining how the Spirit-sign authorizes what he says about Jesus.
payload.title: John questioned and John testifying
